title: People and device pairing
lead: Implement people, device pairing, the long-lived cookie, and revocation (ADR 0010, requirement U7).
boundary: **Not in this slice:** multi-household accounts, passwords, OAuth.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Unpaired devices must not use larder. A non-technical household member must never see a login screen after pairing. Requirement `added_by` attribution needs a Person.

sections.heading: Owner input
sections.body: None. Settled in the S06 interview (2026-10-13); see the flow details in ADR 0010.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Tokens: generate with `secrets`, store only SHA-256 hashes, compare in constant time.
2. People: at startup, sync config people into the `person` mirror. Insert new names, and set `active = 0` on names no longer in config (never delete). Raise `ConfigError` when config names no admin. Existing web tests add an admin to their config.
3. Migration `0002_pairing.sql`: a pairing-token table (token hash, person, kind bootstrap/pair, created, expires (null for bootstrap), used). Pairing state goes through `auth_db.py`.
4. Bootstrap: at startup, while no admin has an active device, replace any unused bootstrap token with a new one and log `/pair/<token>` with a hint to open it on larder's usual address. The token has no expiry and is single use. Its page lists the config admins to pick from.
5. CLI: `python -m larder pair --person NAME` creates a pairing token for any config person and prints `/pair/<token>`.
6. Pairing: the admin devices page picks a person and creates a pairing token (10 minutes, single use). It shows the full link (built from the request host via the trusted proxy) and an inline SVG QR code from `segno`. Opening the link sets the device cookie bound to that person.
7. Add `segno` to `requirements.in` and regenerate the hashed pins. Confirm its license is FLOSS (expected BSD-3) before pinning, and list it in AGENTS.md Dependencies.
8. Cookie: `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Secure` when the request scheme is https (via the trusted proxy), `Max-Age` of 1 year, re-issued when `last_seen` is updated (throttled).
9. A `before_request` guard maps the cookie to an active device of an active person. Otherwise it serves `unpaired.html` (HTTP 401, no app data). `/healthz`, `/pair/...` and static files are exempt.
10. Admin devices page: list, rename, revoke. Admin pages return 403 to members, and admin links are hidden for them.
11. CSRF tokens on state-changing forms (stdlib `secrets` + session).

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- Auth tests pass. `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` are clean.
- ADR 0010 flow details match the behavior.
- Manual run: start with an admin in config, pair a desktop browser from the logged bootstrap link, pair a second browser by link from the admin page, revoke it, and see the unpaired page.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Commit only when the owner asks; no AI attribution.
